THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY RAJESH RAI K. J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

These appeals directed against the judgment and award dated 29.11.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Humnabad, in MVC Nos.409/2017 and NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB 410/2017, as such, they are taken up together for common disposal.

2. MFA No.200328/2020 filed by the Insurance Company and MFA No.200753/2019 filed by the claimants are arising out of MVC No.410/2017, wherein the Tribunal allowed the claim petition filed by the claimants in part and granted Compensation of Rs.15,20,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization of compensation amount.
3.

Similarly, MFA No.202598/2019 filed by the Insurance Company and MFA No.201649/2019 filed by the claimants are arising out of MVC No.409/2017 wherein the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.19,00,300/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization of compensation amount.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB 4.

The factual matrix of the case in brief is that on 15.01.2015 at about 10.00 p.m., the deceased Shanthkumar had been to Zaheerabad in car bearing registration No.KA-39/M-1267 for his personal work after completion of the work, the deceased along with his two friends by name Rajkumar and Tanaji were proceeding towards Humnabad from Zaheerabad and when they came infront of KEB Jyoti And Ors vs Bhaskar Yadav And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152748532/
6 power house at Hudgi village on NH-09 road at that time, a lorry bearing registration No.AP-28/
TA-6190 came from opposite direction, driven by its driver with high speed and in rash and negligent manner, dashed to the said car, as a result, Rajkumar died on the spot and others sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: Soon after the accident, though injured were shifted to Government Hospital Humnabad, and thereafter, to Hyderabad for higher treatment, deceased-Shantkumar succumbed to the injuries on 04.02.2015.

As such, the legal heirs of deceased Rajkumar filed MVC No.410/2017 and the legal heirs of deceased Shanthkumar filed MVC No.409/2017 NC:
2024:KHC-K:4938-DB before the Tribunal claiming compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
5. After issuance of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear.
Hence, he was placed exparte in both the cases.
The respondent-Insurance Company appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement in both the cases denying the averments made in the claim petitions.
6. On the basis of pleadings of rival parties, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
7. In order to prove the claim petition before the Tribunal, petitioner No.1 in MVC No.410/2017 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as per Exs.P1 to P12.

On the other hand,
the respondents have not examined any witness nor marked any documents on their behalf.
8. Whereas in MVC No.409/2017, one Vijaykumar S/o Kashinath Metre was examined as PW.1 and got - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB marked 53 documents as per Exs.P1 to P53.
On the other hand, the respondents have not examined any witness nor marked any documents on their behalf.
9. After assessment of oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petitions filed by the respective parties and awarded the compensation as stated supra.
The challenge to the same is lis before this Court.
10. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the insurance company in both the cases.

11. It is the primary contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company in MFA No.200328/2020 arising out of MVC No.410/2017 that the tribunal totally erred while considering the income of the deceased.

The Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month though the tribunal ought to have taken the income of the deceased at the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB rate of Rs.8,000/- per month.
She would contend that the petitioners have failed to produce any such documents to prove the income of the deceased.

In such Jyoti And Ors vs Bhaskar Yadav And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152748532/
7 circumstances, the tribunal erred while considering the income.

entities.text: Jyoti And Ors vs Bhaskar Yadav And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners in MFA No.200753/2019 arising out of MVC No.410/2017 would contend that the deceased was a driver and he was earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly taken the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the appeal filed by the insurance company and to enhance the compensation awarded in MVC No.410/2017.

13. Learned counsel for the insurance company in MFA No.202598/2019 arising out of MVC No.409/2017 would contend that the Tribunal has erred while deducting the income towards personal expenses of the deceased.
Since the mother of the deceased died during the pendency of the claim petition, the Tribunal ought to have deducted 1/3rd of the income instead of 1/4th.
She would - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB also contend that father, brother and sister could not be considered as dependents.
On these grounds, she prays to allow the appeal.

14. Per Contra, learned counsel for the petitioners in MFA No.201649/2019 arising out of MVC No.409/2017 would contend that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.6,000/- per month which is on the lower side.
Further, the Tribunal has rightly deducted income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
In such circumstances, he prays to dismiss the appeal filed by the insurance company and to allow the appeal filed by the petitioners.
15. We have perused the entire evidence and material placed on record.
On careful perusal of the evidence on record, the accident in question and involvement of the offending vehicle which was insured - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB with respondent No.2 is not in dispute.
Hence, the only point that arises for our consideration in these appeals is with regard to quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
16. As could be seen from the records, the petitioners in MVC No.410/2017 have failed to produce any such documents to substantiate the income of the deceased.
Though it is contended that the deceased was driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, they have not produced any such documents.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has taken notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month.
The Tribunal ought to have taken the notional income as per the chart provided by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority.
In terms of the chart, for the accident of the year 2015, the notional income of the deceased will have to be taken at Rs.8,000/- per month.

To the aforesaid amount, as the deceased was aged 32 years, 40% of the said amount has to be Jyoti And Ors vs Bhaskar Yadav And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152748532/
8

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.11,200/-.

Since there are four petitioners, we deem it appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the said income towards personal expenses of the deceased and therefore, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.8,400/-.

Taking into account the age of the deceased which was 32 years at the time of accident, multiplier of 16 has to be adopted as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,12,800/- (Rs.8,400/- x 12 x 16) on account of loss of dependency.

17. Further, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others reported in (2018)
18 SCC 130,
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB each petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.

sentences.text: The petitioners are four in number, hence, the compensation towards loss of consortium would be Rs.1,60,000/- (40,000 x 4).
In addition, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
18 . Thus, in all, the petitioners in MVC No.410/2017 are entitled to a sum of Rs.18,02,800/- as against Rs.15,20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,82,800/-.
19. As could be seen from the records, the petitioners in MVC No.409/2017 have failed to produce any such documents to substantiate the income of the deceased-Shantkumar.
Though it is contended that the deceased was driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, they have not produced any such documents.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has taken - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.
The Tribunal ought to have taken the notional income as per the chart provided by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority.
In terms of the chart, for the accident of the year 2015, the notional income of the deceased will have to be taken at Rs.8,000/- per month.

To the aforesaid amount, as the deceased was aged 25 years, 40% of the said amount has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.11,200/- .

Since the deceased was bachelor, we deem Jyoti And Ors vs Bhaskar Yadav And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152748532/
9 it appropriate to deduct 50% of the said income towards personal expenses of the deceased and therefore, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.5,600/-.

sentences.text: Taking into account the age of the deceased which was 25 years at the time of accident, multiplier of 18 has to be adopted as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra).
Therefore, the - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.12,09,600/- (Rs.5,600/- x 12 x 18) on account of loss of dependency.
20. Further, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma (supra), each petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.
The petitioners are three in number, hence, the compensation towards loss of consortium would be Rs.1,20,000/- (40,000 x 3).
In addition, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
21. The petitioners have produced medical bills in order to show that the petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.9,76,300/- towards medical expenses of the deceased- Shantkumar.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses is retained.
22. Thus, in all, the petitioners in MVC No.409/2017 are entitled to a sum of Rs.23,35,900/- as against - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB Rs.19,00,300/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,35,600/-.

23. Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeals filed by the Insurance Company in MFA Nos.200328/2020 and 202598/2019 are dismissed.
ii. The appeals filed by the petitioners in MFA Nos.200753/2019 and 201649/2019 are allowed in part.
iii. The impugned judgment and award dated 29.11.2018 in MVC Nos.410/2017 and 409/2017 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Humnabad is modified.
iv. Petitioners in MVC No.410/2017 are entitled to a sum of Rs.18,02,800/- as against Rs.15,20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,82,800/-.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month though the tribunal ought to have taken the income of the deceased at the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB rate of Rs.8,000/- per month.
She would contend that the petitioners have failed to produce any such documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly taken the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the appeal filed by the insurance company and to enhance the compensation awarded in MVC No.410/2017.
Since the mother of the deceased died during the pendency of the claim petition, the Tribunal ought to have deducted 1/3rd of the income instead of 1/4th.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Though it is contended that the deceased was driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, they have not produced any such documents.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has taken notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month.
The Tribunal ought to have taken the notional income as per the chart provided by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority.
Taking into account the age of the deceased which was 32 years at the time of accident, multiplier of 16 has to be adopted as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.
Taking into account the age of the deceased which was 25 years at the time of accident, multiplier of 18 has to be adopted as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra).
opennyai_summary.decision:
Since there are four petitioners, we deem it appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the said income towards personal expenses of the deceased and therefore, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.8,400/-.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,12,800/- (Rs.8,400/- x 12 x 16) on account of loss of dependency.
The petitioners are four in number, hence, the compensation towards loss of consortium would be Rs.1,60,000/- (40,000 x 4).
In addition, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
18 . Thus, in all, the petitioners in MVC No.410/2017 are entitled to a sum of Rs.18,02,800/- as against Rs.15,20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.12,09,600/- (Rs.5,600/- x 12 x 18) on account of loss of dependency.
20. Further, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma (supra), each petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.
The petitioners are three in number, hence, the compensation towards loss of consortium would be Rs.1,20,000/- (40,000 x 3).
In addition, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses is retained.
22. Thus, in all, the petitioners in MVC No.409/2017 are entitled to a sum of Rs.23,35,900/- as against - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4938-DB Rs.19,00,300/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,35,600/-.

ORDER i.
The appeals filed by the Insurance Company in MFA Nos.200328/2020 and 202598/2019 are dismissed.

iii. The impugned judgment and award dated 29.11.2018 in MVC Nos.410/2017 and 409/2017 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Humnabad is modified.
iv. Petitioners in MVC No.410/2017 are entitled to a sum of Rs.18,02,800/- as against Rs.15,20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,82,800/-.
